why: Benchmark section 6: product-shaped screens (an inbox pane, a record window, a builder, a week calendar, a wizard) are too product-shaped to freeze as npm API, and today that tier is recipes no compiler checks (`docs/recipes/board.md`, `saved-views.md`, `view-switch.md`, the `chat-thread` files). The eject machinery is the base: `basalt-ui eject` (src/cli/eject/index.ts) writes the file, a merge base under `.basalt/base/`, a ledger row in `.basalt/manifest.json` (`EjectedRow`: path, fromVersion, seedDigest, reason, origin seed, adopted or local; src/cli/eject/ledger.ts, src/cli/manifest.ts), and `sync` merges three ways (`planEjected`, `applyEjected`, src/cli/sync/three-way.ts, on `git merge-file`). It handles primitives from src/ui only (`SEED_DIR`, src/cli/merge/seed.ts). The five reference pages (apps/playground/src/routes/ref/: parts.tsx, notes.tsx, suppliers.$id.tsx, settings.tsx, -new-order.tsx) are the first blocks. docs/v3/DIRECTION.md section 6 refused an `add` verb; the owner approved the benchmark that adds this tier, and this row reverses that line.

change: Read first: docs/v3/issues/bench/README.md (owner direction, decisions, how to use the reference) and docs/v3/BENCHMARK-ACCORDEE-BLUEPRINT.md, sections 2 and 11. Decided: (1) A block is a directory under packages/basalt-ui/blocks/<name>/ with its files and a small descriptor (name, files, the subpaths it imports, the ports its data comes through); it imports only public basalt-ui subpaths and takes its data through typed props or loaders, with its fixture beside it for the playground and shots only. (2) `basalt-ui add <block>` copies it into the app (default under src/blocks/, configurable), writes a merge base and a ledger row with origin `block` beside the eject rows, and never overwrites an existing file; `basalt-ui add --list` prints the blocks with one line each. (3) `basalt-ui sync` merges a changed block three ways as it does an ejected primitive; a local edit survives an upgrade or stops on a conflict with markers, never silently lost. Blocks do not count against the eject budget. (4) The five reference pages become blocks: list page, notes list with record surface, record page, settings page, create flow; the playground routes render the block source, so one source is linted, typechecked, shot and shipped. (5) The basalt-design skill answers "which page do I copy" with `basalt-ui add <block>`. (6) Document the promotion rule: a block two consumers run unchanged is promoted to a composite. Rows that land after this one ship their proof page as a block.
reference: Benchmark section 6 (tiers table) and section 7 (an exemplar per archetype, "a list page copies Invoices"). docs/v3/concepts/primitives-distribution.md section 8: the registry format has no version and no lockfile, and `add --overwrite` destroyed four of four edits: never overwrite. No shots: this row is tooling.
acceptance: `basalt-ui add <block>` installs a block into a fresh app that then typechecks and lints at error (pack test on the tarball)
An edited block survives `basalt-ui sync` after the block changed upstream, or stops with conflict markers (test on a fixture app)
The five reference pages are blocks and the playground renders them from the block source
The skill names `basalt-ui add` for each archetype
out_of_scope: A public registry or a library site (after 3.0). Converting recipes beyond the reference pages. Blocks for the calendar, inbox, chat and canvas (their rows ship them).
proof: A transcript of `basalt-ui add` and `basalt-ui sync` on a fixture app in the PR, and the pack test output.
commits: Conventional, empty scope, packages/basalt-ui/** in its own commits. Never feat!: and no BREAKING CHANGE footer (docs/release.md). A changed or removed export updates migrations/areas and the generated docs in the same PR.
